title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using AI deepfakes to impersonate trusted professionals and family members in scams across Georgia and South Florida. The scams include voice cloning to target immigrants by posing as immigration attorneys, fake photographs, spoofed phone numbers, and other identity impersonations used in romance scams, investment fraud, and emergency schemes. This is a failure of detection at the point of contact: people receiving communications cannot reliably distinguish AI-generated impersonations from authentic ones because the technology has become sophisticated enough to replicate voices and likenesses convincingly.

These scams would require intervention at multiple levels to prevent. Social media platforms and communication services would need to detect and block deepfake content and spoofed numbers before victims encounter them. Financial institutions would need to verify requests for urgent transfers through independent channels. Victims themselves would need a way to authenticate the person contacting them that does not rely on voice, appearance, or familiar communication patterns. The reports do not establish whether any particular platform, service provider, or institution failed to implement available safeguards, only that these scams are occurring at scale.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to commit sophisticated scams across Georgia and South Florida. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report found that Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year, with Florida reporting 350 complaints totaling $39.9 million and Georgia reporting 71 complaints totaling $10.4 million. Scammers use deepfake technology to clone voices from social media, create fake photographs, spoof phone numbers, and impersonate trusted individuals like family members or professionals. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam.

These AI-powered scams are making common fraud schemes harder to recognize, including romance scams, fake investment opportunities, emergency calls, and grandparent scams. Financial institutions warn customers that AI-generated impersonations are becoming increasingly difficult to detect. Experts recommend establishing code words with family members to verify identity, pausing before responding to urgent requests, and verifying communications through known phone numbers. Authorities suggest that as AI tools become cheaper and more accessible, verification rather than quick action will be consumers' strongest defense against these evolving scams.
